title: Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2026)
provenanceNote: Comprehensive NCCN Guidelines Version 1.2026 clinical navigator for Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (upper endoscopy with push or balloon-assisted enteroscopy or video capsule endoscopy after confirming patency, multiphase CT/MR enterography plus CT chest/abdomen/pelvis, histopathologic confirmation with primary site duodenum/jejunum/ileum, universal MMR/MSI testing with Lynch syndrome assessment, comprehensive molecular profiling for KRAS/NRAS/BRAF/HER2/NTRK, baseline CBC/CMP plus CEA and CA 19-9) -> Stage and Biomarker Stratification (localized resectable Stage I-III vs advanced/metastatic dMMR/MSI-H vs advanced/metastatic pMMR/MSS vs subsequent-line/relapsed) -> Resectable complete surgical resection with regional mesenteric lymphadenectomy followed by adjuvant mFOLFOX6/CAPOX for Stage III or high-risk Stage II (BALLAD trial) -> dMMR/MSI-H first-line pembrolizumab or nivolumab with or without ipilimumab (KEYNOTE-158/KEYNOTE-177, CheckMate-142) -> pMMR/MSS first-line mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX with or without bevacizumab, FOLFOXIRI for select fit patients -> Subsequent-line FOLFIRI with or without bevacizumab, trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) with or without bevacizumab, or biomarker-targeted therapy (larotrectinib/entrectinib for NTRK fusions, encorafenib plus cetuximab for BRAF V600E, trastuzumab plus tucatinib for HER2-amplified disease). References StewardMD Standard Protocols. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma Version 1.2026.

a.text: Video capsule endoscopy requires confirmed luminal patency (patency capsule or cross-sectional imaging) to avoid capsule retention at an obstructing small bowel tumor; push enteroscopy, single/double-balloon-assisted enteroscopy, and EGD cover duodenal and proximal jejunal lesions.

b.text: Universal MMR/MSI testing by IHC for MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, and PMS2 (with MSI PCR or NGS confirmation where indicated). Small bowel adenocarcinoma has a high dMMR/MSI-H rate (~15-20%) with strong Lynch syndrome association; refer dMMR cases for genetic counseling and germline testing.

c.text: Adjuvant chemotherapy for resected Stage III (node-positive) or high-risk Stage II (T4, perforation, obstruction, close/positive margins, inadequate nodal sampling) small bowel adenocarcinoma: mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX for 6 months per the BALLAD trial paradigm; duodenal primaries resected by pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple), jejunal/ileal primaries by segmental small bowel resection with wide regional mesenteric lymphadenectomy.

d.text: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks or 400 mg IV every 6 weeks (KEYNOTE-158/KEYNOTE-177 paradigm) or nivolumab 240 mg IV every 2 weeks (or 480 mg every 4 weeks) with or without ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks (CheckMate-142 paradigm) produces exceptional durable responses in dMMR/MSI-H small bowel tumors; monitor for immune-related adverse events.

e.text: First-line pMMR/MSS metastatic therapy uses an oxaliplatin-based doublet: mFOLFOX6 (oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-FU 400 mg/m2 bolus plus 2400 mg/m2 46h infusion every 14 days) or CAPOX (capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 BID days 1-14 plus oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 every 21 days) with or without bevacizumab (5 mg/kg q14d with FOLFOX or 7.5 mg/kg q21d with CAPOX); FOLFOXIRI is reserved for select fit patients.

f.text: Subsequent-line therapy: FOLFIRI (irinotecan 180 mg/m2, leucovorin, 5-FU bolus/infusion every 14 days) with or without bevacizumab; trifluridine/tipiracil (TAS-102) 35 mg/m2 BID days 1-5 and 8-12 every 28 days with or without bevacizumab; biomarker-targeted options include larotrectinib/entrectinib for NTRK fusions, encorafenib plus cetuximab for BRAF V600E, and trastuzumab plus tucatinib for HER2-amplified disease.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the clinical workup before stage and biomarker stratification. Confirm endoscopic and imaging assessment, histology with primary site, universal MMR/MSI status, comprehensive molecular profile, and baseline labs with tumor markers.
bullets: Upper endoscopy (EGD) with push enteroscopy, balloon-assisted enteroscopy, or video capsule endoscopy (after confirming patency)
Cross-sectional imaging: multiphase contrast-enhanced CT enterography or MR enterography, plus CT chest/abdomen/pelvis
Histopathologic confirmation of adenocarcinoma with primary anatomic site: duodenum (55%), jejunum (30%), or ileum (15%)
Mandatory universal MMR / MSI testing (IHC for MLH1, MSH2, MSH6, PMS2; high ~15-20% Lynch syndrome association)
Comprehensive molecular testing: KRAS, NRAS, BRAF V600E, HER2 amplification, and NTRK gene fusions
Baseline laboratory assessment: CBC, CMP, and serum tumor markers (CEA, CA 19-9)

nodes.name: Stage and Biomarker Stratification
nodes.title: Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma: Stage and Biomarker Stratification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Assign resectability (Stage I-III vs metastatic) and MMR/MSI status plus treatment line; the group selects the surgical-adjuvant, dMMR immunotherapy, pMMR chemotherapy, or subsequent-line pathway.
nodes.path: Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma / Stage and Biomarker Stratification
bullets: Localized / resectable disease: Stage I-III (T1-T4, N0-N2, M0) amenable to complete surgical resection with negative margins and regional lymphadenectomy.
Advanced / metastatic dMMR / MSI-H disease: unresectable or M1 with mismatch repair deficiency or microsatellite instability-high status.
Advanced / metastatic pMMR / MSS disease: unresectable or M1 with mismatch repair proficient or microsatellite stable status.
Subsequent-line / relapsed disease: progression after first-line systemic therapy or relapse after prior definitive treatment.

nodes.name: Resectable Treatment
nodes.title: Stage I-III Resectable: Surgery Then Adjuvant mFOLFOX6/CAPOX
nodes.description: Complete surgical resection with negative margins and regional mesenteric lymphadenectomy followed by adjuvant oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy for Stage III or high-risk Stage II disease.
bullets: Complete surgical resection with negative margins and regional mesenteric lymphadenectomy: Pancreaticoduodenectomy / Whipple for duodenal primaries; segmental small bowel resection with wide lymphadenectomy for jejunum/ileum primaries.
Adjuvant chemotherapy for Stage III (node-positive) or high-risk Stage II (T4, perforation, obstruction): 6 months of mFOLFOX6 (Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2 plus Leucovorin plus 5-FU bolus/infusion).
Alternative adjuvant option: CAPOX (Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 BID days 1-14 plus Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 every 21 days; BALLAD trial paradigm).
Surveillance after definitive therapy: history, physical examination, CBC/CMP, CEA and CA 19-9, plus cross-sectional imaging per NCCN schedule; offer clinical trial enrollment.

nodes.name: dMMR/MSI-H Metastatic Treatment
nodes.title: dMMR/MSI-H Metastatic: Pembrolizumab or Nivolumab Immunotherapy
nodes.description: First-line systemic immunotherapy for advanced or metastatic dMMR/MSI-H small bowel adenocarcinoma with exceptional durable objective response rates.
nodes.path: Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma / Metastatic dMMR-MSI-H / Systemic Therapy
bullets: First-line systemic immunotherapy: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV every 3 weeks or 400 mg IV every 6 weeks (KEYNOTE-158 / KEYNOTE-177).
Alternative: Nivolumab 240 mg every 2 weeks (or 480 mg every 4 weeks) with or without Ipilimumab 1 mg/kg every 6 weeks (CheckMate-142).
Exceptional durable objective response rates in dMMR small bowel tumors; continue until disease progression or unacceptable toxicity with immune-related adverse event monitoring.
Confirm dMMR/MSI-H status, refer for Lynch syndrome genetic counseling, and offer clinical trial enrollment.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w (or Nivolumab +/- Ipilimumab) Immunotherapy

nodes.name: pMMR/MSS Metastatic Treatment
nodes.title: pMMR/MSS Metastatic: mFOLFOX6 or CAPOX With or Without Bevacizumab
nodes.description: First-line oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy doublet with or without bevacizumab for advanced or metastatic pMMR/MSS small bowel adenocarcinoma.
nodes.path: Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma / Metastatic pMMR-MSS / Systemic Therapy
bullets: First-line oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy doublet: mFOLFOX6 (Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m2, Leucovorin 400 mg/m2, 5-FU 400 mg/m2 bolus plus 2400 mg/m2 46h continuous infusion every 14 days).
Alternative doublet: CAPOX (Capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 BID days 1-14 plus Oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1 every 21 days) with or without Bevacizumab 5 mg/kg IV every 14 days (or 7.5 mg/kg every 21 days).
Bevacizumab may be added to mFOLFOX6 (5 mg/kg IV every 14 days); alternative: FOLFOXIRI for select fit patients.
Restage with cross-sectional imaging every 8-12 weeks on systemic therapy; offer clinical trial enrollment at every line.
Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.

nodes.path: Small Bowel Adenocarcinoma / Subsequent-Line / Systemic Therapy
bullets: FOLFIRI (Irinotecan 180 mg/m2, Leucovorin, 5-FU bolus/infusion every 14 days) with or without Bevacizumab.
Trifluridine/Tipiracil (TAS-102 35 mg/m2 BID days 1-5 and 8-12 every 28 days) with or without Bevacizumab.
Biomarker-targeted options: Larotrectinib/Entrectinib for NTRK fusions; Encorafenib plus Cetuximab for BRAF V600E; Trastuzumab plus Tucatinib for HER2-amplified disease.
Repeat molecular profiling at progression to confirm actionable targets; offer clinical trial enrollment at every line.
